evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ASPRV1 Cause Dominantly Inherited Ichthyosis.
evidence.snippet: Three different heterozygous ASPRV1 missense mutations in four unrelated ichthyosis kindreds segregate with disease and disrupt protein residues within close proximity to each other and autocatalytic cleavage sites.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline missense variants in ASPRV1, including p.(Lys199Glu), p.(Arg311Pro) and p.(Pro314Thr), alter residues that lie close to one another and to the autocatalytic cleavage sites of SASPase. ASPRV1 knockout mice do not develop lamellar ichthyosis, so the dominant effect is thought to be more than simple loss of activity (dominant negative or neomorphic); the cited abstracts do not settle which.

nodes.description: Active SASPase cleaves the linker peptides of profilaggrin in the granular layer to release filaggrin monomers, which bundle keratin filaments and are later degraded into natural moisturizing factor. Mutant SASPase fails to process filaggrin, so profilaggrin is left unprocessed. The conformance to the cornification module's envelope node rests on loss of the filaggrin keratin matrix; whether lamellar lipid delivery is also affected is not shown for ASPRV1.

nodes.description: Knockout of SASPase on a hairless background gives dry, rough skin with a thicker, less hydrated stratum corneum, aberrant profilaggrin intermediates and markedly reduced filaggrin.

The stratum corneum is thickened and retained as large adherent scale. In SASPase-deficient hairless mice it is thicker and less hydrated; in patients the corresponding clinical finding is lamellar scaling with palmoplantar keratoderma. The mouse supports the processing-to-hydration step but does not reproduce lamellar ichthyosis (see the discussion).
